facts.topic: Vercel Hobby — function max duration (Fluid compute)
facts.fact: With Fluid compute (default for projects created after 2025-04-23), Hobby functions have a default AND maximum duration of 300 s; exceeding it returns 504 FUNCTION_INVOCATION_TIMEOUT. The 800 s / 1800 s extended maxima are Pro/Enterprise only. Legacy non-Fluid Hobby functions: default 10 s, max 60 s. Our routes export maxDuration = 60 (app/api/generate/route.ts:14, app/api/jobs/[id]/route.ts:14, app/api/b/[slug]/route.ts:23, app/api/b/[slug]/card/route.ts:18, app/api/tg/[botId]/route.ts:19), which is valid on both models.
facts.source: https://vercel.com/docs/functions/limitations and https://vercel.com/changelog/higher-defaults-and-limits-for-vercel-functions-running-fluid-compute (via WebSearch, 2026-11-08; vercel.com is not fetchable from this sandbox, so numbers come from search excerpts of the official pages)
facts.impactForUs: Budget is adequate: text waits 50 s and createTask 45 s with retries (lib/server/gateway.ts TIMEOUT_MS / RETRY_BUDGET_MS) inside 60 s. If Fluid is ON (must be verified in Vercel project settings), maxDuration can be raised to up to 300 s for /api/jobs/[id] so the after() download of up to 100 MB (gateway.ts MAX_RESULT_BYTES) never gets cut; if the project is on legacy non-Fluid, 60 s is the hard ceiling and a slow 50–100 MB kie download would be killed, leaving the job in 'storing' until reclaimed 3 min later (job-rules.ts STORING_RECLAIM_AFTER_MS). Same at 10 and 50 users; severity medium.

facts.topic: Vercel Hobby — memory / CPU
facts.fact: Hobby functions get 2 GB memory / 1 vCPU (Standard CPU), not configurable; Pro/Enterprise 4 GB.
facts.impactForUs: storeJobResult buffers the whole result in memory (gateway.ts downloadResult collects chunks up to 100 MB) — fits in 2 GB even with Fluid in-function concurrency handling several downloads at once (10 users: ≤10 × ~15 MB videos; 50 users: ≤50 × 15 MB = 750 MB worst case in one instance — tight but under 2 GB). Low severity; a streaming upload to Supabase would remove the risk.

facts.topic: Vercel — function concurrency
facts.fact: Functions auto-scale up to 30,000 concurrent executions on Hobby and Pro (100,000+ Enterprise). No separate lower per-project Hobby default was found in the docs. With Fluid compute, Node.js instances handle multiple requests concurrently (optimized concurrency) and new instances start only when none has spare capacity.
facts.impactForUs: 10 students (≤~4 req/s of polling + chat) or 50 students (≤~20 req/s) are far below any compute concurrency limit; Vercel is not the bottleneck. The bottlenecks are n8n concurrency and kie rate limits (see below).

facts.topic: Vercel Hobby — included monthly quotas and overage behaviour
facts.fact: Hobby includes per month: 4 hours Active CPU, 360 GB-hrs Provisioned Memory, 1,000,000 function invocations, 100 GB Fast Data Transfer, 1,000,000 CDN/edge requests. Hobby cannot buy overages: 'if you exceed your usage limits on the Hobby plan, you will have to wait until 30 days have passed before you can use the feature again' and Hobby teams 'will be paused when they exceed the included free tier usage'; unpausing requires support and is not automatic.
facts.impactForUs: Estimated lesson load: 10 students → ≈9,000 /api/jobs polls (75 min / 5 s, GenerateClient.ts POLL_MS) + proxy.ts invocations (counted separately as function invocations) ≈ 20k invocations, ≈0.1 CPU-hour; 50 students ≈ 100k invocations, ≈0.5 CPU-hour. One lesson fits; a month with 8+ 50-student sessions approaches the 4 CPU-hour cap. Media bytes are served from Supabase signed URLs, not Vercel, so 100 GB transfer is safe. The real risk is a pause mid-lesson once a cap is crossed — critical because recovery takes days. Fix: move to Pro before selling (also required by ToS, next fact) and watch Usage dashboard.

facts.topic: Vercel Hobby — commercial use forbidden
facts.fact: Fair Use Guidelines: 'Hobby teams are restricted to non-commercial personal use only. All commercial usage of the platform requires either a Pro or Enterprise plan.' Commercial = any deployment used for financial gain of anyone involved (taking payments, advertising a product/service, being paid to build or host). ToS: 'You shall only use the Services under a Hobby plan for your personal or non-commercial use.' Commercial use is a listed reason deployments get paused.
facts.impactForUs: The owner sells the course and intends to sell the platform to other centres → the production deployment is commercial and violates Hobby terms. Failure scenario (10 or 50 users): Vercel pauses the team during a paid workshop; all students see an error page. Severity critical (lesson breaks, reputational). Fix: upgrade to Pro ($20/seat/mo) before Monday if the course is paid; Pro also gives cron (replace lazy polling), 800 s functions, overage billing instead of pausing.

facts.topic: Vercel — 4.5 MB request/response body limit
facts.fact: Vercel Functions cap request bodies at 4.5 MB (413 FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE) and non-streamed responses at 4.5 MB (FUNCTION_RESPONSE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE); the limit applies to all plans and streaming does not lift the request-side limit. Recommended pattern: client uploads directly to storage via a signed URL.
facts.impactForUs: Confirmed safe: montage MP4 (up to 50 MB, lib/platform/montage/types.ts:79) goes browser → Supabase via createSignedUploadUrl (lib/server/studio.ts:383–388); /api/generate caps body at 64 KB (app/api/generate/route.ts:16,28); studio routes use readJson with 64 KB / 1 KB limits (lib/server/studio.ts:84; app/api/studio/save/[id]/complete/route.ts:15); no Server Action accepts files (app/(platform)/**/actions.ts — no File/formData usage). Results are fetched by the server from kie and pushed to Supabase, never returned through a function body. No finding; low severity.

facts.topic: Next.js 16 — Server Actions body limit and CSRF
facts.fact: Server Action requests are capped at 1 MB by default (serverActions.bodySizeLimit); Next.js compares Origin to Host (X-Forwarded-Host) and rejects mismatches; actions are POSTs to the page route and must do their own auth.
facts.impactForUs: Our largest action payloads are bot soul 4,000 + knowledge 8,000 chars (lib/server/bot/limits.ts:9–10) and quiz answers — well under 1 MB. No change needed.

facts.topic: Next.js 16 — cacheComponents and dynamic pages
facts.fact: With cacheComponents: true (next.config.ts:92) data fetching is dynamic by default; Next prerenders a static shell and streams request-time parts (anything reading cookies()/headers()) inside <Suspense>. Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime (no runtime export). Enabling it 'can surface build errors for uncached data outside of <Suspense>'. after() runs for the route's maxDuration and 'will be executed even if the response didn't complete successfully'; under serverless it relies on waitUntil.
facts.source: node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/cacheComponents.md; 01-app/02-guides/upgrading/version-16.md:1258; 01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/after.md ('Duration', 'Good to know', 'Reference: supporting after for serverless platforms')
facts.impactForUs: Every authenticated page view still costs one function invocation (dynamic part), so cacheComponents does not reduce the per-student load; it only speeds first paint. Route Handlers (/api/*) are plain dynamic functions and scale per invocation. after() in job-progress.ts:158 is bounded by maxDuration=60 of /api/jobs/[id]; Vercel honours it via waitUntil. Keep maxDuration ≥ expected download+upload time.

facts.topic: Next.js 16 — proxy.ts runtime and cost
facts.fact: proxy (ex-middleware) runs ONLY on the Node.js runtime; edge is not supported and cannot be configured (version-16.md:600). On Vercel, Routing Middleware runs as full Vercel Functions on Fluid compute and is billed as invocations + Active CPU; the old 50 ms CPU limit applied only to Edge Middleware.
facts.impactForUs: proxy.ts matcher covers /app, /teach, /admin, /login, /b, and all /api except /api/tg (proxy.ts:71), so every 5 s job poll triggers proxy (supabase.auth.getClaims(), proxy.ts:57, which may do a network token refresh) plus the route — doubling invocations and adding latency. 10 users: ~18k extra invocations/lesson; 50 users: ~90k. Within quota but wasteful. Fix (medium): exclude /api/jobs and /api/generate from the matcher (routes already call authorize() in the DAL) or keep but ensure getClaims stays local (no DB).

facts.topic: In-memory caches under Fluid compute
facts.fact: Fluid instances are long-lived and serve many concurrent requests; module-level state persists per instance and is NOT shared across instances. lib/server/prices.ts:61–90 keeps a 60 s TTL price cache per instance; invalidatePriceCache() only clears the instance that served the admin request. lib/server/rate-limit.ts stores counters in Postgres via rate_limit_hit RPC and fails open on DB error (rate-limit.ts:37–45).
facts.source: Code: lib/server/prices.ts:61–90, lib/server/rate-limit.ts:30–46; Vercel Fluid docs https://vercel.com/docs/fluid-compute (WebSearch, 2026-11-08)
facts.impactForUs: Price cache: after an admin price change other warm instances serve stale prices ≤60 s; create_job (supabase/migrations/20261101200000_init.sql:574–580) rejects charging a student below the list price but will charge a stale HIGHER price for up to 60 s. Low severity; acceptable, or add price_list.updated_at check. Rate limit: DB-backed → correct across instances; 100 attempts/IP/15 min (rate-limit.ts:21) comfortably covers 10 or 50 students logging in from one Wi-Fi (50 students × ~2 attempts = 100 — exactly the cap; raise ip limit to 300 for 50-person rooms, medium). Fail-open is a documented trade-off.

facts.topic: Kie.ai — request rate limit
facts.fact: Official docs: default limit of 20 new generation requests per 10 seconds per account ('typically supports 100+ concurrent running tasks'); 'KIE does not set a strict concurrency limit on running tasks'; requests over the limit get HTTP 429 and 'rejected requests will not enter the queue'. Higher limits on request to support. Errors on /api/v1/* can arrive with HTTP 200 and the error in the body 'code' field.
facts.source: https://docs.kie.ai/ and https://kie.ai/getting-started (WebSearch, 2026-11-08; docs.kie.ai is not fetchable from this sandbox)
facts.impactForUs: 10 students: even a simultaneous click burst (10 createTask + text) stays under 20/10 s. 50 students: a synchronized 'everyone generate now' burst of 50 exceeds 20 per 10 s → ~30 get 429; gateway.ts isTransientFailure treats 429 as retryable with backoff 1.5/3/5/8 s (RETRY_DELAYS_MS) inside a 45 s budget, so the burst drains in ~25 s but each retry is an extra n8n execution. Status polling (recordInfo) is a separate endpoint; its limit is not documented (unresolved). Severity medium at 50; fix: teacher staggers the 'go' signal, or add a per-group token bucket in create_job. Also verify the n8n 'Normalize Response' node checks the body 'code' field, not only HTTP status.

facts.topic: Kie.ai — 'Resources are tight' 502/503
facts.fact: No official documentation of the 'Resources are tight, please try again later' message or of 502 behaviour was found; the only evidence is the owner's own observation on 2026-11-05 (gateway.ts comment: kie returned 502/503/429 with that text, quickly and without creating a task; Haiku ~10% success vs Kimi K3 ~95% that day; docs/kie-gateway.md 'Изменения 5 ноября').
facts.source: lib/server/gateway.ts (comment above RETRY_DELAYS_MS), docs/kie-gateway.md; WebSearch for the exact phrase returned no kie.ai source (2026-11-08)
facts.impactForUs: Treat as transient upstream overload. Current handling (5 attempts with model rotation Haiku→Kimi→Kimi→Haiku→GPT-6 Luna for text; 4 attempts for createTask) is reasonable. Risk at 10/50 users: during an overload window every student's chat message turns into up to 5 n8n executions and up to 50 s latency; at 50 users that is up to 250 executions per round of messages and 50 concurrent n8n webhook executions — this is where n8n concurrency (next fact) breaks first. Severity high during kie incidents; fix: cap retries to 3 during lessons, show 'kie busy' message early, pre-warm by checking balance/health before the lesson.

facts.topic: n8n Cloud — plan quotas and concurrency
facts.fact: n8n.io/pricing (2026): Starter €20/mo — 2,500 workflow executions/month and 5 concurrent executions; Pro €50/mo — 10,000 executions (older table said 25k; n8n SaaS page and support FAQ say 10k) and 20 (comparison table) / 'up to 50' concurrent; Business 40k executions; Enterprise 200+ concurrent. Executions reset on the 1st of the month; Pro-2 can buy extra executions. Over-limit production executions are queued FIFO until capacity frees (concurrency control docs). One webhook call = one execution regardless of duration.
facts.source: https://n8n.io/pricing/, https://n8n.io/saas/, https://support.n8n.io/article/can-i-add-more-executions, https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/scaling/concurrency-control/ (WebSearch, 2026-11-08; n8n.io not fetchable from sandbox; Pro concurrency figure conflicts 20 vs 50)
facts.impactForUs: The gateway workflow 'ИИ-старт: шлюз KIE для курса' (v21nopocrCSYPBGd) responds via 'Respond to Webhook', so each execution holds a concurrency slot for the whole kie call (text 3–10 s, createTask up to 40 s KIE POST timeout, status ~0.3 s observed in execution log ids 506–555). 10 students sending chat at once = 10 concurrent > Starter's 5 → half queue ~5–10 s extra; tolerable. 50 students = 50 concurrent → queue depth 45 × ~5 s ≈ 45 s wait, exceeding the platform's 50 s text timeout (gateway.ts TIMEOUT_MS.text) → gateway_timeout → refund + error for many students. Severity high at 50 on Starter, medium on Pro (20 concurrent). Fix: Pro plan or self-hosted n8n with N8N_CONCURRENCY_PRODUCTION_LIMIT raised, and reduce slot time (shorter KIE POST timeout, async callback for createTask).

facts.topic: n8n executions estimate per 75-minute lesson
facts.fact: Per student (code-derived): ~15 chat messages × 1.3 retry factor ≈ 20 executions; 2 images × (1 create + ~4 status polls at 5 s for 12–20 s jobs) ≈ 10; 2 videos × (1 create + 18–36 polls for 90 s–3 min jobs, server-side claim every ≥5 s via claim_job_poll, init.sql:617–626, while the tab is visible) ≈ 40–75; bot-lesson messages ≈ 20 (each bot reply = 1 execution, lib/server/bot/brain.ts:202; bot card = create + polls every 3 s, BotChat.tsx:31). Total ≈ 90–125 executions per student per lesson.
facts.source: Code: components/platform/GenerateClient.ts:12,79–92 (5 s polling, paused when tab hidden), lib/server/job-rules.ts:13 (GATEWAY_POLL_INTERVAL_SEC=5), supabase/migrations/20261101200000_init.sql:617–626, lib/server/bot/brain.ts:202, components/platform/BotChat.tsx:31–32; observed durations from n8n execution log (ids 506–555, 2026-11-06)
facts.impactForUs: 10 students ≈ 900–1,250 executions per lesson → one lesson uses ~40–50% of a Starter month (2,500); 2–3 lessons/month exhaust Starter and the webhook stops responding → every generation fails (critical, money-safe because refunds happen but lesson breaks). 50 students ≈ 4,500–6,250 per workshop → exceeds Starter in one session and uses ~50–60% of Pro (10k). Fix: Pro plan at minimum; cut executions by raising poll interval to 10 s for video (halves polls), using kie callbacks (1 execution per job instead of 20–40), or moving status polling off n8n (call kie recordInfo directly from Vercel with the key as a Vercel secret).

facts.topic: n8n gateway workflow state (owner's instance)
facts.fact: Workflow v21nopocrCSYPBGd is active (published 2026-11-05, version 'Запасная текстовая модель Kimi K3'), 9 nodes, webhook trigger with 'Respond to Webhook', no executionTimeout in settings (settings: executionOrder v1, availableInMCP true). 253 executions recorded since 2026-11-01, all recent ones 'success'; status polls take ~0.26–0.30 s, text calls 1–5 s, longest observed 22 s (id 548).
facts.impactForUs: Baseline healthy. Missing a workflow-level execution timeout means a hung kie HTTP call can hold a concurrency slot until n8n's default timeout; set workflow settings → Timeout Workflow ≈ 55 s to free slots. The owner's n8n Cloud plan tier was not visible via MCP — must be checked in the n8n dashboard (unresolved).

facts.topic: Per-user job concurrency guard (code)
facts.fact: create_job rejects a 6th simultaneous active job per user ('too_many_jobs' when ≥5 jobs in queued/submitted/storing, init.sql:571–573).
facts.impactForUs: Caps gateway load at ≤5 active jobs per student → ≤50 active jobs at 10 students (≤10 status polls/s), ≤250 at 50 students (≤50 polls/s ≈ 50 n8n executions per 5 s window, each ~0.3 s ≈ 3 concurrent) — polling alone fits even Starter concurrency; the pressure comes from long text/createTask executions. Consider lowering to 3 for students.

facts.topic: Vercel cold starts
facts.fact: On Node.js 20+ production deployments Vercel pre-compiles function code (bytecode caching) on all plans. Pre-warmed instances ('scale to one') are documented for paid plans; Hobby pre-warming is not clearly stated (sources conflict).
facts.impactForUs: First login of the day may see a 1–3 s cold start; after that Fluid reuses instances, so 10 or 50 students logging in within 2 minutes share warm instances. Low severity; the teacher can open the site 5 minutes before class.

facts.topic: Auth rate limit — /auth/v1/token (sign-in with password AND refresh) is one per-IP token bucket
facts.fact: Supabase Auth limits `/auth/v1/token` per IP address: 1800 requests per hour, token bucket with capacity (burst) 30; bucket refills at the configured rate (1800/h = 30/min = 0.5/s). When empty → HTTP 429. In the GoTrue source the password grant does NOT get its own limiter: `internal/api/token.go` sets `limiter := a.limiterOpts.Token` and the `case "password": // set above` branch keeps it, same as `refresh_token`; only `web3` switches limiter. `internal/api/apilimiter/apilimiter.go` builds `Token` as `gc.RateLimitTokenRefresh/(60*5)` with burst 30, TTL 1h; `internal/conf/configuration.go` default `RateLimitTokenRefresh float64 default:"150"` (150 per 5 min = 1800/h). So password sign-ins and refreshes from one IP share the same 30-token bucket. Docs table marks it 'Customizable: No', but the same page's Management API PATCH example includes `rate_limit_token_refresh`, so it may be adjustable via `PATCH /v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth`.
facts.source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/rate-limits (via Supabase docs MCP, 2026-11-08); https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod#auth-rate-limits (2026-11-08); GoTrue source raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/auth/master/internal/api/token.go, internal/api/apilimiter/apilimiter.go, internal/conf/configuration.go (2026-11-08)
facts.impactForUs: app/(platform)/login/actions.ts:49 calls signInWithPassword server-side, so GoTrue keys the bucket on the Vercel function's egress IP, not the student's. 10 students in 2 min: ≤10 (+ a few wrong-password retries) requests → inside the 30 burst, no problem even if all share one IP. 50 students in 2 min: capacity ≈ 30 burst + 60 refilled over 120 s ≈ 90 requests if all from ONE IP → OK only if ≤ ~40 extra failed attempts; if logins cluster into ~30 s the capacity is 30+15=45 < 50 and the last ~5–10 students get 429, which actions.ts:52 maps to TOO_MANY ('Подождите пару минут'). Severity: high at 50 (some students see errors; lesson start delayed), low at 10. Fix: (1) in actions.ts, on `error.status === 429` retry once after ~2 s before surfacing TOO_MANY, and show a message that says 'попробуйте через 10 секунд' rather than 'пару минут'; (2) have the teacher log students in two waves of 25 ≥ 1 min apart (documented procedure in setup.md); (3) on Pro, raise `rate_limit_token_refresh` via Management API (verify it applies); (4) do NOT expect client-side sign-in to fix this: the whole room shares one public IP, so a browser-side signInWithPassword would hit exactly the same per-IP bucket.

facts.topic: Which IP GoTrue sees for server-side calls; supabase-js/ssr do not forward the client IP
facts.fact: GoTrue determines the IP as: `sbff.GetIPAddress(r)` (the `Sb-Forwarded-For` header, only when the project flag `security_sb_forwarded_for_enabled` is on) else first valid entry of `X-Forwarded-For`, else `RemoteAddr` (internal/utilities/request.go). Supabase docs: 'By default, Supabase Auth uses the IP address of the client for rate limiting... To use a forwarded IP address set the `Sb-Forwarded-For` header to the end-user IP address and make a request with a secret API key. Publishable API keys and legacy anon/service_role keys are not supported. IP address forwarding must be explicitly enabled for new projects (Authentication > Rate Limits > IP Address Forwarding).' supabase-js sends only `X-Client-Info` by default (packages/core/supabase-js/src/lib/constants.ts DEFAULT_HEADERS) and @supabase/ssr adds `X-Client-Info: supabase-ssr/<v> createServerClient` (node_modules/@supabase/ssr/dist/main/createServerClient.js:29); neither sends X-Forwarded-For or the client IP.
facts.impactForUs: lib/server/supabase/server.ts:18 creates the login client with the publishable key, so even if we set `sb-forwarded-for` from headers() it would be ignored per docs. Our own IP-based counter (lib/server/rate-limit.ts:17-22, actions.ts:43-46) correctly compensates for brute-force protection, and it keys on the Vercel-provided `x-forwarded-for` (lib/server/bot/ratelimit.ts:36-40), which is the real student IP. Severity: medium (design constraint, not a bug). Fix options: (a) keep server-side login and accept Vercel egress IPs (see Vercel fact — they are dynamic, which actually spreads load over several buckets); (b) if 429s are observed, enable 'IP Address Forwarding' in Authentication > Rate Limits and perform ONLY the `signInWithPassword` call with a secret-key client that sets `global.headers['sb-forwarded-for'] = clientIp`, then hand the returned session to the cookie-based publishable client via `auth.setSession()`; never use that secret-key client for `.from('profiles')` (actions.ts:57) or RLS is bypassed.

facts.topic: Classroom NAT: all students share one public IP regardless of login architecture
facts.fact: Supabase per-IP limits key on the IP the Auth server sees. From the classroom, 10–50 browsers behind one router present the same public IPv4 (or one IPv6 /64). Vercel functions, by contrast, make outbound requests 'from a dynamic range of addresses... each invocation can exit from a different server'; a fixed outbound IP (Static IPs) exists only on Pro/Enterprise and excludes Routing Middleware.
facts.source: https://vercel.com/guides/how-to-allowlist-deployment-ip-address and https://vercel.com/docs/connectivity/static-ips (via WebSearch summary, 2026-11-08); Supabase rate-limits doc (2026-11-08)
facts.impactForUs: Moving sign-in to the browser (createBrowserClient) would NOT raise capacity for a single room: 50 students → one IP → same 30-burst/1800-h bucket on /token; it only isolates different rooms from each other. Server-side login on Vercel Hobby spreads requests over a dynamic egress range, so in practice the per-IP bucket is probably hit less often than from the room — but the pool size per region is undocumented, so treat it as 'likely helps, not guaranteed'. At 10: no issue either way. At 50: plan the two-wave login and the 429 retry (previous fact). Severity: high at 50 if ignored. Our own limiter lib/server/rate-limit.ts:21 allows 100 attempts per IP per 15 min: 50 students with one typo each = 100 → the next attempt from the room is blocked for 15 minutes. Raise LOGIN_LIMITS.ip to ≥300 for IPv4 (or key the account limit only and keep IP limit as a sanity cap of e.g. 600/15 min).

facts.topic: Token refresh load during a 75-minute lesson
facts.fact: Access tokens default to 3600 s (`JWT.Exp` set to 3600 in ApplyDefaults; supabase/config.toml:40 `jwt_expiry = 3600`). Supabase recommends keeping 1 h and never below 5 min. Refresh requests hit the same `/auth/v1/token` per-IP bucket (1800/h, burst 30). auth-js refreshes proactively (AUTO_REFRESH_TICK 30 s, EXPIRY_MARGIN = threshold × tick) only in browser clients; server clients refresh lazily when the token is near expiry during getClaims().
facts.impactForUs: proxy.ts:57 runs getClaims() on every matched request (/app, /teach, /admin, /login, /b, /api except /api/tg). A refresh happens roughly once per student per hour → 10 or 50 refreshes spread across 75 min from Vercel IPs: negligible against 1800/h. Severity: low. No change needed; do not lower JWT expiry below 1 h (it multiplies refreshes against the same bucket as logins).

facts.topic: Refresh token rotation, reuse interval, two tabs / two devices
facts.fact: Refresh token rotation is on by default (`RefreshTokenRotationEnabled default:"true"`); a refresh token can be reused within the reuse interval, default 10 seconds (config.toml:42 `refresh_token_reuse_interval = 10`; docs: 'we do not recommend changing this value'). Two exceptions prevent false revocation: reuse within 10 s, and using the parent of the currently active token returns the active token. Any other reuse marks the whole session's refresh tokens revoked. 'By default [a session] lasts indefinitely and a user can have an unlimited number of active sessions on as many devices.' Time-boxed sessions, inactivity timeout and 'Single session per user' are Pro-only and off by default; enforcement happens at next refresh, so effective duration = setting + JWT expiry.
facts.impactForUs: Two tabs in one browser share the `sb-*` cookie; at expiry both tabs' requests cause proxy.ts:57 refreshes with the same refresh token — covered by the 10 s reuse window and the parent-token exception, so no random logouts. Same login on two devices (our test with two browsers): two independent sessions, each with its own refresh chain → both keep working; this stays true at 10 or 50 students. Risk only if someone later enables 'Single session per user' (Pro): the earlier device is logged out within ≤1 h. Severity: low. Recommendation: leave rotation/reuse defaults; do not enable single-session; in docs/platform/setup.md note that one card can be used on two devices and that a logout on one device does not log out the other (signOut default scope is global in auth-js — verify desired scope; actions.ts:69 uses default).

facts.topic: Free vs Pro — compute and connections
facts.fact: Nano (Free): shared CPU, up to 0.5 GB RAM, recommended max DB 500 MB, 60 Postgres max connections, 200 pooler clients. Micro (default on paid): 2-core shared ARM, 1 GB RAM, ~$10/mo (covered by $10 compute credits on Pro), recommended ≤10 GB DB, 60 connections, 200 pooler clients. Small ~$15/mo, 2 GB, 90/400. Nano is not auto-upgraded when moving to Pro and is billed like Micro; compute change takes <2 min downtime. Pooler and connection limits are hard-coded per compute size.
facts.impactForUs: The app talks to Postgres only via PostgREST/Auth/Storage (createClient / createAdminClient), never with direct pg connections, so the 60-connection cap is consumed by Supabase's own services and is not hit by 10 or 50 browsers. The real Free-plan risk is Nano's shared CPU/0.5 GB RAM under 50 concurrent users calling security-definer money functions + polling (lib/server/job-progress.ts) — undocumented, must be load-tested. Severity: medium on Free, low on Pro/Micro. Fix: run on Pro and after upgrading manually switch compute Nano→Micro in Settings > Compute and Disk (not automatic); keep polling intervals modest.

facts.topic: Free vs Pro — database size, pausing, backups
facts.fact: Free projects enter read-only mode when *database size* exceeds 500 MB (disk 1 GB); errors look like `cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction`. Pro: 8 GB disk included, auto-expands +50% at 90% (max 4 resizes per 24 h; at 95% with quota exhausted → read-only), $0.125/GB-month beyond 8 GB. Free projects 'that show low activity over a 7-day period' are paused (warning e-mail ~1 week before); restore via dashboard within 90 days (older doc copies say 1 year); paid projects are never paused. Free: database backups not downloadable; Pro: daily backups, PITR add-on. Fair Use on Free: notification, grace period, then restrictions (pausing, read-only, 402 on all API requests).
facts.impactForUs: Workshops are weekly or less: on Free the project can be paused between sessions → Monday morning every login fails until the owner clicks 'Resume project' (several minutes). Severity: critical on Free (lesson breaks), none on Pro. Our tables (jobs, bot_messages, stars ledger) at 50 students grow slowly; 500 MB is months away, but a read-only flip would break every generation (insert into jobs/ledger) at once. Fix: Pro plan before the first paid workshop; if staying on Free for a test, open the dashboard or hit the API daily in the week before, and check DB size in Observability > Database.

facts.topic: Free vs Pro — egress, storage size, MAU quotas and prices
facts.fact: Unified egress quota: Free 5 GB uncached + 5 GB cached; Pro/Team 250 GB + 250 GB; overage $0.09/GB uncached, $0.03/GB cached (cached = Smart CDN hits, Storage only; Smart CDN is Pro+). Storage size: Free 1 GB, Pro 100 GB, overage $0.0213/GB-month. MAU: Free 50,000, Pro 100,000, overage $0.00325/MAU. Free orgs may run 2 active free projects. Pro: $25/mo + $10 compute credits, Spend Cap on by default (over quota → notification + grace period, then restrictions unless cap disabled). Egress is counted for Database (PostgREST responses), Auth, Storage downloads, Realtime, Functions; uploads (ingress) are not egress.
facts.impactForUs: MAU is irrelevant (50 students ≪ 50,000). Egress is the Free-plan killer: generated videos/images are served via signed URLs (lib/server/storage.ts:34 createSignedUrls, TTL 3600 s at storage.ts:23) — uncached unless Smart CDN (Pro). 10 students × 3 videos (~3–5 MB each) × a few plays ≈ 0.5 GB/lesson; 50 students ≈ 2–3 GB/lesson plus montage downloads → Free's 5 GB uncached quota is exhausted in 1–2 workshops → grace period then 402/restrictions mid-course. Severity: critical on Free, low on Pro (250 GB). Fix: Pro; set `cacheControl` on uploads (storage.ts:51 already 3600) and reuse the same signed URL within a page session so Smart CDN can hit.

facts.topic: Storage cost of 50 students × 50 MB montages per week
facts.fact: Arithmetic from the official prices above: 50 × 50 MB = 2.5 GB uploaded per week (~10–11 GB/month). Uploads are free (ingress). Storage size accumulates: ~10 GB/month → Free 1 GB quota exceeded in week 1; Pro 100 GB quota lasts ~9–10 months, then $0.0213/GB-month (an extra 10 GB ≈ $0.21/month). Egress: if each montage is viewed/downloaded ~3× (student preview, teacher, share) ≈ 7.5 GB/week ≈ 30 GB/month uncached → Free quota (5 GB) blown immediately; Pro stays inside 250 GB → $0 extra. Total Pro cost for this pattern ≈ the $25 plan (compute covered by credits) until storage passes 100 GB.
facts.impactForUs: Severity: critical on Free (service restriction), low on Pro. Fix: add a retention rule (delete montage MP4s and intermediate media older than N weeks, or cap per-student storage) so Storage size does not grow unbounded; this also bounds egress from re-downloads. studio.ts:383 (createSignedUploadUrl with upsert) already overwrites same path, which helps.

facts.topic: Storage file size limits (global and bucket)
facts.fact: Global file size limit: Free cannot exceed 50 MB; Pro/Team up to 500 GB (set in Storage Settings). Per-bucket `file_size_limit` cannot be higher than the global limit. Standard (single request) upload is recommended for files up to ~6 MB; resumable (TUS) uploads are recommended for files that may exceed 6 MB or on unstable networks, chunk size must be 6 MB, upload URL valid 24 h, and the direct storage host `https://<ref>.storage.supabase.co` should be used for large files. Signed upload URLs (`createSignedUploadUrl`) are valid for 2 hours; their token can also be passed as `x-signature` to the resumable endpoint.
facts.impactForUs: supabase/migrations/20261101200000_init.sql:893-894 creates bucket `media` with 52428800 (50 MB) — the Free ceiling; after moving to Pro the *global* limit must also be ≥50 MB (it is by default on Free, verify after upgrade). The montage flow (lib/server/studio.ts:383) hands the browser a signed upload URL used with a single PUT: a 30–50 MB PUT over classroom Wi-Fi with 50 students uploading simultaneously will sometimes fail and must restart from zero (storage.ts:46 'upload_failed'). Severity: medium at 50 (some students retry), low at 10. Fix: switch the browser upload to TUS (tus-js-client, `x-signature` = signed-upload token, 6 MB chunks, direct storage hostname) or at least add automatic retry with progress UI; keep bucket limit at 50 MB.

facts.topic: Signed URL limits
facts.fact: `createSignedUrl(s)` take `expiresIn` in seconds; no maximum expiry or per-call rate limit is documented. Signed URLs stay valid until expiry regardless of key changes; with Smart CDN (Pro) each unique `?token=` is a separate cache key, so a freshly signed URL is always a cache miss; cached copies can outlive token expiry until the cache TTL ends; deleting the object purges all cached entries within ~60 s.
facts.impactForUs: lib/server/storage.ts:27-34 signs in chunks per request with TTL 1 h; gallery pages of 24 items (gallery.ts:25) re-sign on every render → every open of the gallery is a CDN miss and full uncached egress at 10 and 50 students. Severity: low (cost/perf only). Fix: cache signed URLs per (user, path) for ~50 min server-side or in the client, so repeated views reuse the same token; keep sensitive content behind short TTLs.

facts.topic: PostgREST Max Rows (default 1000) and pagination
facts.fact: Supabase projects return at most 1,000 rows per Data API request by default ('Max Rows' in Project Settings > Data API; PostgREST `db-max-rows`). A `.limit()` larger than Max Rows is silently capped; use `.range(from, to)` to page. Supabase recommends keeping the value low to bound payload size.
facts.impactForUs: Already handled where it matters: lib/server/group-reports.ts:13-24 pages with PAGE=1000 and `range(from, from+PAGE-1)`; gallery uses 24-row pages (gallery.ts:25-39); lesson-progress limit 80. Two soft spots: (1) lib/server/bot/dal.ts:174 `.limit(1000)` on bot_leads — leads beyond 1000 are silently dropped from the teacher view (low, far future); (2) group-reports.ts:24 stops when `data.length < PAGE` — if an admin lowers Max Rows below 1000 in the dashboard, pagination ends after the first page and reports under-count (low). Fix: read PAGE from a single constant documented in setup.md as 'must equal Max Rows', or page until an empty result. At 10/50 students no table approaches 1000 rows per query. The owner's recollection of '10 000 rows' is wrong: it is 1,000.

facts.topic: Email/OTP/signup rate limits (not on our hot path)
facts.fact: Endpoints that send e-mail (`/signup`, `/recover`, `/user` email change) are limited project-wide to a low number per hour with the built-in SMTP (changeable only with custom SMTP; going-into-prod says custom-SMTP default is 30 new users/hour). OTP 360/h project-wide, 60 s between requests per user; anonymous sign-ins 30/h per IP; `/verify` 360/h per IP burst 30; MFA 15/min per IP.
facts.impactForUs: Students have synthetic @students.example.com logins created by the teacher through the admin API (lib/server/accounts.ts), so no confirmation e-mails, OTPs or recover flows are sent during class; these limits do not bite at 10 or 50. Severity: low. Keep 'Confirm email' irrelevant for admin-created users; if teacher accounts use real e-mail + password reset, expect the 60 s per-user window and the hourly project cap.

facts.topic: Vercel egress IP and inbound client IP
facts.fact: Vercel Functions send outbound requests from a dynamic range of addresses that can differ per invocation; Static IPs (fixed pair per region) are a Pro/Enterprise feature and do not cover Routing Middleware. Vercel sets `x-forwarded-for` on inbound requests to the real client IP (platform-controlled, spoofed values are overwritten).
facts.source: https://vercel.com/guides/how-to-allowlist-deployment-ip-address and https://vercel.com/docs/connectivity/static-ips (via WebSearch summary, 2026-11-08); comment in lib/server/bot/ratelimit.ts:33-35
facts.impactForUs: Our per-student IP limiter (actions.ts:43, ratelimit.ts:36) is sound on Vercel. On Hobby we cannot buy a static egress IP, so the Supabase per-IP bucket for server-side logins is keyed on whichever Vercel IP the invocation uses — undocumented pool size; could be one IP for a warm instance handling many logins. Severity: medium at 50 (uncertainty), low at 10. Fix: the 429 retry/backoff in actions.ts and two-wave login procedure; optionally log `error.status` and timestamps for login failures (audit.ts) to measure during the first 50-person workshop.

facts.topic: Server-side auth caching hazard
facts.fact: Supabase warns that when a session is refreshed server-side the new tokens go out via Set-Cookie; if that response is cached by a CDN/ISR another user can receive someone else's session. `setAll` receives cache headers (Cache-Control/Expires/Pragma) that must be applied to the response in the proxy.
facts.impactForUs: proxy.ts:51 already copies those headers onto the response, and lib/server/supabase/server.ts:23-31 wraps setAll in try/catch per the official pattern. Severity: none (verified correct). Keep this when refactoring; Next.js 16 cacheComponents must not cache any route that reads cookies().

findings.title: Group-page star stats read star_ledger without pagination: silently capped at 1000 rows (PostgREST Max Rows)
findings.evidence: getGroupStarStats selects `delta, reason` from star_ledger with `.in('user_id', students)` and NO .limit/.range (teacher.ts:369-375). PostgREST returns at most Max Rows (1000, supabase/config.toml:13, project default per [research]) and supabase-js does not signal truncation. The result is summed in JS (teacher.ts:380-383) and shown as «Роздано / Потрачено» on the group page (page.tsx:103-108). By contrast group-reports.ts:13-27 pages with PAGE=1000, so the author knew about the cap but this query was missed. Every chat message = 1 ledger row (debit), every image/video = 1-2 rows (debit + possible refund), every bot reply = 1 row.
findings.scenario10: 10 students × ~20 chat + 6 media + welcome ≈ 30 rows/lesson → 300 rows/lesson; the 1000-row cap is crossed in lesson 4: from then on «Потрачено» and «Роздано» on the group page under-count silently (the teacher sees budget numbers that stop growing).
findings.scenario50: 50 students × 30 rows ≈ 1500 rows after the FIRST 75-minute workshop → the group page is already wrong at the end of lesson 1; a teacher deciding whether to grant more stars sees spending that is 30-60% too low. With 5 lessons ≈ 7500 rows, the card shows roughly 1/7 of real spending.
findings.fix: Aggregate in SQL instead of fetching rows: add a security-definer RPC `group_star_stats(p_group uuid) returns table(given bigint, spent bigint)` (grant execute to service_role only) that does `select sum(case when reason in ('debit','refund','bot_reply') then -delta else 0 end), sum(case when reason not in (...) then delta else 0 end) from star_ledger l join profiles p on p.id=l.user_id where p.group_id=p_group`, and call it from getGroupStarStats. Interim: reuse fetchAll() from group-reports.ts. Add a lint/grep rule in setup.md: every list query must have .limit()/.range() or go through fetchAll.

findings.title: Group report reads the whole ledger/progress of a group through RLS, evaluating 3 security-definer sub-queries per row; grows linearly with course length
findings.evidence: getGroupReport uses the teacher's RLS client (createClient, group-reports.ts:61) to fetch ALL lesson_progress, quiz_attempts and all debit/refund/bot_reply ledger rows of the group (lines 62-89, paged by 1000). Policies ledger_read / lesson_progress_read are `user_id = auth.uid() or private.teaches_user(user_id)` (init.sql:391-392, 409-410). For a teacher the first branch is false on every row, so Postgres calls teaches_user → teaches_group → is_admin() + a groups⋈profiles EXISTS (init.sql:314-327) for EVERY row. These are SECURITY DEFINER SQL functions, which Postgres cannot inline, so the cost is ~3 index lookups per row and cannot be cached per statement (only the `(select auth.uid())` part is). No index exists on star_ledger(reason) — fine because user_id leads — but the row count itself is the problem. The report page exports no maxDuration (report/page.tsx), so it runs under the default page timeout.
findings.scenario10: After 5 lessons ≈ 1500 ledger rows + ~300 progress rows → 2 PostgREST pages, ~5-6k RLS sub-selects; page loads in 1-3 s. Degraded but works.
findings.scenario50: After 5 lessons ≈ 7-10k ledger rows → 8-10 sequential 1000-row requests (fetchAll is sequential, group-reports.ts:20-25), each paying ~3k function calls plus JSON serialization of 1000 rows; on Nano/Micro shared CPU the report page takes 5-15 s and can hit the Vercel page timeout (10 s on non-Fluid Hobby per [research]) → teacher sees a 504 for the report at the exact moment the course ends and they want to show results to the center.
findings.fix: After getGroup()/assertTeachesGroup has verified the teacher, read report data with createAdminClient() (RLS bypass, same pattern as getGroupStarStats) and aggregate in SQL: one RPC `group_report(p_group)` returning per-student `(user_id, spent_total, spent_today, generations, refunds, bot_replies)` via `group by user_id`, plus a progress query `select user_id, lesson_id, count(*)`. This turns 10 requests × 1000 rows into 2 requests × 50 rows and removes the per-row RLS function calls. Also export `maxDuration = 60` on the report page as a safety net.

findings.title: Every paid spend in a group serializes on one `groups` row lock (lock_for_spend … FOR UPDATE), including guest bot replies — a single hot row for 50 concurrent students
findings.evidence: lock_for_spend does `select g.paused, g.daily_cap … from groups g where g.id = v_group_id for update` whenever p_amount > 0 (hardening.sql:188), i.e. for every create_job (init.sql:561) and every spend_stars bot reply (init.sql:764, p_count_cap=false but the FOR UPDATE still runs). The row lock is held until the RPC transaction commits, so all paid generations and all public /b/[slug] + Telegram bot replies of a group are strictly serialized. While holding the lock, create_job also runs the daily-cap SUM over the group's ledger (hardening.sql:191-194) even though daily_cap was set to 1,000,000 = disabled (group_budget.sql:12-13), then the wallet lock, duplicate check, active-job count, price lookup, insert, update, insert. Lock order is always group → wallet; refund_job locks job → wallet; grant/quiz lock wallet only — no deadlock cycle exists (verified), so this is throughput, not correctness.
findings.scenario10: 10 simultaneous «generate» clicks → 10 transactions queued on the group row, each ~5-15 ms on Micro → worst case ~150 ms extra latency. Invisible.
findings.scenario50: 50 students clicking within the same second (teacher says «go») → 50 serialized transactions, each ~10-30 ms on Nano shared CPU incl. the useless ledger SUM → 0.5-1.5 s queue; during lesson 3 add dozens of guest bot messages per minute hitting the same lock. Still no errors (no statement timeout is hit at these durations), but it is the one place that gets slower the more students a group has, and a long-running transaction holding that lock (e.g. a slow ledger SUM on a large table) would stall every student at once.
findings.fix: (1) Take the group row lock only when a cap is actually enforced: `if p_count_cap and v_cap < 1000000 then … for update else plain select`; or drop FOR UPDATE and read `paused` with a plain select (a pause arriving mid-transaction is harmless). (2) Skip the ledger SUM when daily_cap >= 1000000 and global_daily_cap is null. (3) If global_daily_cap is ever enabled, add `create index star_ledger_created_idx on star_ledger (created_at desc) where reason in ('debit','refund')` — today the global SUM (hardening.sql:201-203) would be a sequential scan on every generation. (4) Keep wallet FOR UPDATE (per-user, correct).

findings.title: A text (chat) job that dies between create_job and complete_job stays `queued` with the debit kept, and is refunded only if the browser later polls that exact job
findings.evidence: runText: create_job debits (generate.ts:294-304), then awaits generateText (up to 50 s budget), then `await completeJob()` (generate.ts:329). rpcBoolean THROWS on any PostgREST error (jobs.ts:280-282); the route catch returns `{error:'server_error'}` WITHOUT jobId (app/api/generate/route.ts:83-88) so the client cannot poll it. The same happens if Vercel kills the function at maxDuration=60 (50 s text budget + DB round trips + cold start is tight, see [research] Fluid vs legacy). There is no sweeper: the only refund path for `queued` is advanceJob on GET /api/jobs/[id] after 3 min (job-progress.ts:126, job-rules.ts QUEUED_WITHOUT_TASK_LIMIT_MS). getLessonState shows only the 6 newest jobs per task (lesson-progress.ts:153,186-189), so a stuck chat message older than 6 messages is never rendered, never polled, never refunded — and it counts forever toward the 5-active-job cap (init.sql:570-573, jobs_open_idx).
findings.scenario10: Rare: one kie overload window with retries pushing a request past 60 s → 1-2 students lose 1-3★ each (not noticed) and carry a permanent phantom «active job»; after 5 such incidents over the course a student gets `too_many_jobs` (429) on every generation with nothing visible in progress.
findings.scenario50: During a kie incident (owner observed ~10% Haiku success on 5 Nov) 50 students × several chat retries → dozens of functions near the 60 s ceiling; a few percent die → several students end the workshop with phantom queued jobs and lost stars; by the next workshop a handful hit `too_many_jobs` and the teacher cannot see why (jobs page shows nothing active).
findings.fix: Add a per-user sweeper RPC `reclaim_stale_jobs(p_user uuid)` (security definer, service_role only) that refunds `queued` jobs with gateway_task_id null older than 3 min and `storing` older than 60 min for that user (reusing refund_job), and call it from getLessonState / listMyGallery / before the too_many_jobs path (or inside create_job itself before counting active jobs: `perform public.refund_job(id,'gateway_lost') for stale queued rows of p_user`). Also make the `too_many_jobs` count ignore `queued` rows older than 3 min. Return `jobId` in the 500 response of runText so the client can poll it.

findings.title: Teacher «Боты группы» page issues 2 COUNT queries per bot (N+1): 100 parallel PostgREST calls for a 50-student group
findings.evidence: listGroupBots maps every bot to `Promise.all([count bot_leads, count bot_messages … gte weekAgo])` (bot/dal.ts:274-285). Indexes bot_leads_bot_idx and bot_messages_bot_day_idx (init.sql:253,239) make each count cheap, but the number of HTTP round trips is 2×bots, fired concurrently from one serverless invocation into PostgREST's connection pool.
findings.scenario10: 10 bots → 20 counts in parallel; ~200-400 ms. Fine.
findings.scenario50: 50 bots → 100 concurrent requests from one function; PostgREST on Nano queues them against its small DB pool while 50 students are generating → the page takes 1-3 s and briefly starves other requests; still renders.
findings.fix: One grouped query each: `select bot_id, count(*) from bot_leads where bot_id in (...) group by bot_id` and the same for bot_messages with the week filter (either via an RPC/view or `select('bot_id', { count: 'exact' })` is not groupable, so use an RPC `group_bot_counters(p_bot_ids uuid[], p_since timestamptz)`). 2 requests instead of 2N.

findings.title: Bot leads list hard-capped at 1000 (limit(1000) = Max Rows) with no paging; export/UI silently drops older leads
findings.evidence: listMyLeads uses `.limit(1000)` (bot/dal.ts:174) which equals PostgREST Max Rows; nothing tells the owner that more exist. BOT_LIMITS.leadsPerBotPerDay = 50 (limits.ts:19), so 1000 leads ≈ 20 days at the cap — reachable only for adult/teacher bots that stay live after the course.
findings.scenario10: Not reachable during the course.
findings.scenario50: Not reachable during the course; only a long-lived promoted bot could exceed it, then the oldest leads vanish from the owner's list and CSV without warning.
findings.fix: Page with .range() and a «show more» or iterate with fetchAll for CSV export; or cap display at 200 newest and show total via `count: 'exact', head: true` (already done for leadsCount).

findings.title: Price cache is per serverless instance (60 s TTL); invalidatePriceCache only clears the instance that served the admin — but create_job's server-side floor makes it money-safe
findings.evidence: Module-level `cache` (prices.ts:62) lives per Fluid instance; invalidatePriceCache (prices.ts:88) is local. create_job re-reads price_list inside the transaction and rejects a student price below the list minimum (init.sql:574-581), so a stale LOWER price fails safely with `forbidden`; a stale HIGHER price is charged for ≤60 s.
findings.scenario10: Admin lowers a price mid-lesson → for ≤60 s some students see `forbidden` (403) instead of the new price, or pay the old higher price. Rare, bounded.
findings.scenario50: Same, more instances → more students see a 403 blip for up to a minute after a price change.
findings.fix: Acceptable as is; document «не менять прайс во время урока» in setup.md, or add `price_list.updated_at` max() check (1 cheap query) before trusting the cache.

findings.title: Classroom login IP limiter (100 attempts / 15 min per IP) is DB-backed and correct, but the shared-IP budget is 2 attempts per student at 50 students
findings.evidence: rate_limit_hit stores one row per attempt in private.rate_limit_hits under an advisory lock per key (hardening.sql:136-151) — correct across Vercel instances (unlike an in-memory counter) and indexed (hardening.sql:116-117). LOGIN_LIMITS.ip = 100/15 min (rate-limit.ts:200); the whole room shares one public IP ([research]). The account counter is reset on success (actions.ts:55) but the IP counter is not. Failed attempts also consume the Supabase per-IP token bucket ([research]).
findings.scenario10: 10 students × up to 10 typos = 100 → practically never hit.
findings.scenario50: 50 students × 2 typos (card passwords like kiwi-raketa-sova-42 are mistyped often on phones) = 100 → the 101st attempt from the room returns TOO_MANY for 15 minutes for EVERYONE, including students who have not logged in yet. Lesson start blocked.
findings.fix: Raise LOGIN_LIMITS.ip to 600/15 min for IPv4 (brute force is still bounded by the 20/15 min per-account limit), and call resetAttempts for the IP key as well on success — or better, count only FAILED attempts against the IP key (take the hit after a failed signInWithPassword, not before). The advisory lock per IP key serializes the room's logins but each call is ~1 ms; fine.

findings.title: Signed URLs are re-created on every gallery/lesson render (no reuse), making each page view a Storage API burst and an uncached egress hit
findings.evidence: toJobViews → signMediaPaths → createSignedUrls in chunks of 100 (storage.ts:33-36) per render; gallery pages re-sign 24-50 paths per view, getLessonState re-signs up to 80 jobs' files on every lesson page load (lesson-progress.ts:171-192), studio lists sign up to 300 paths (studio.ts:230). Each fresh `?token=` is a new CDN cache key ([research] Smart CDN).
findings.scenario10: ~10 Storage sign calls/min, egress ~0.5 GB per lesson. Fine on Pro, eats Free's 5 GB quota in ~10 lessons.
findings.scenario50: Gallery/lesson re-renders by 50 students ≈ 50-100 sign calls/min plus full re-download of every thumbnail/video on each view; ≈2-3 GB egress per workshop ([research]) — fine on Pro, breaks Free within 2 workshops.
findings.fix: Cache signed URLs server-side per path for ~50 min (Map in the admin module or `unstable_cache` keyed by path+TTL bucket) so repeat views reuse the same token and CDN entry; keep 1 h TTL. Lower lesson-page signing to only the jobs actually rendered (6 per task) by filtering before toJobViews — lesson-progress.ts:191 already trims to 6 per task, so only gallery/studio remain.

findings.title: No retention/cleanup for jobs, bot_messages, star_ledger, audit_log, rate_limit_hits or Storage objects — unbounded growth toward Free-plan read-only mode
findings.evidence: Only two cleanup paths exist: rate_limit_hits (2 % random delete of >1 day, hardening.sql:141-143) and abandoned montage uploads (studio.ts:297-323). jobs.params (≤32 KB jsonb) and result_text (≤20 KB) are kept forever; bot_messages (≤4 KB content) accumulate per guest; Storage keeps every result and montage. Free plan flips to read-only at 500 MB DB ([research]) which would fail every create_job/insert at once.
findings.scenario10: ~300 jobs + 500 messages per lesson → a few MB per lesson; years of headroom on the DB; Storage grows ~0.5-1 GB per lesson (videos + montages) → Free 1 GB Storage quota in week 1-2.
findings.scenario50: ~1500 jobs + 2500 messages + up to 2.5 GB Storage per workshop; DB still only tens of MB per month, but Storage passes 100 GB (Pro quota) in ~9 months.
findings.fix: Add a retention routine run by the owner (SQL in setup.md or an admin action): delete Storage objects + null storage_path for jobs older than N weeks after group.ends_on, delete bot_messages older than 30 days, keep star_ledger and audit_log (append-only by design). Document the Free-plan read-only threshold.

findings.title: PostgREST Max Rows is an invisible contract: group-reports pagination stops early if the dashboard value is lowered below 1000
findings.evidence: fetchAll stops when `data.length < PAGE` with PAGE=1000 (group-reports.ts:13,24). PostgREST silently returns min(limit, Max Rows) rows; if an admin sets Max Rows to e.g. 500 in Project Settings → Data API, every page returns 500 < 1000 and the loop exits after the first page, under-counting. Local config pins 1000 (config.toml:13) but the production value is set in the dashboard, not in the repo.
findings.scenario10: Only if someone changes the dashboard setting; then report totals are 1-page truncated.
findings.scenario50: Same; with 7-10k ledger rows the report would show roughly 1/10 of spending.

okChecked: Connection model: all DB access goes through supabase-js over PostgREST/Auth/Storage HTTP (lib/server/supabase/admin.ts:14-21 singleton service-role client; server.ts:37-57 per-request cookie client; proxy.ts:100-116). No pg/pg-pool, no direct Postgres connections anywhere in lib/ or app/ — the 60-connection cap (Nano/Micro) cannot be exhausted by 10 or 50 browsers; only PostgREST's own pool is involved.

Lazy poller double-advance is prevented in SQL: claim_job_poll (init.sql:617-626) is a conditional UPDATE on status='submitted' and last_polled_at ≤ now−5 s, so two tabs/devices polling the same job get exactly one `true` per 5 s window; begin_job_storing (init.sql:629-637) is a conditional UPDATE submitted→storing (or storing older than 3 min), so only one handler enters after(storeJobResult) (job-progress.ts:157-158). Both verified by pgTAP tests 002_wallet.test.sql:75-87.

Double refund is impossible: refund_job (init.sql:659-689) locks the jobs row FOR UPDATE, exits early for done/failed, and the partial unique index star_ledger_job_once (job_id, reason) (init.sql:166) plus the explicit `not exists refund` check make a second refund a no-op; test 002:64-70 covers it. complete_job after a late refund is rejected (status filter), and refund after complete returns 0 (test 002:90-93).

create_job idempotency under concurrency: the idempotency key is checked before and again after acquiring the wallet row lock (init.sql:551, 564), and (user_id, idempotency_key) is UNIQUE (init.sql:161); two concurrent clicks with the same key cannot double-charge. Student price floor and staff-only model checks are re-validated inside the transaction (init.sql:574-581).

Lock ordering is acyclic: lock_for_spend takes group → wallet; refund_job takes job → wallet; grant_stars, record_quiz_attempt take wallet only; apply_student_meta takes profile row then updates wallet. No transaction acquires wallet before group or job, so no deadlock cycle exists between create_job, spend_stars, refund_job, grant_stars and the quiz bonus.

Bot message limits are atomic: insert_bot_message (hardening.sql:39-102) takes pg_advisory_xact_lock per bot and per sender, checks dedupe_key / telegram_update_id, counts hour/day windows and inserts in one transaction; unique indexes bot_messages_dedupe_once and bot_messages_tg_update_once back it. Counts use bot_messages_ip_idx (partial on ip_hash) and bot_messages_bot_day_idx.

Hot-path indexes exist for every query I traced: jobs by (user_id, created_at desc) [listMyGallery, getLessonState, savesToday, card count, closeStaleUploads], jobs by (group_id, created_at desc) [shared/teacher gallery], partial jobs_open_idx (user_id) where status active [too_many_jobs count], jobs.id PK [loadJob/poll], jobs.gateway_task_id unique, (user_id, idempotency_key) unique; star_ledger (user_id, created_at desc) [student home, reports, group daily-cap SUM via profiles_group_idx], partial (user_id, idempotency_key) [spend_stars/grant_stars idempotency, alreadyCharged], partial (job_id, reason); bot_messages (bot_id, conversation_id, created_at desc) [loadHistory]; bot_leads (bot_id, created_at desc); profiles (group_id); groups (teacher_id); lesson_progress PK (user_id, lesson_id, step); quiz_attempts unique (user_id, lesson_id); rate_limit_hits (key, hit_at) and (hit_at).

Pagination is correct where volume is realistic: gallery pages of 24 with range(from, to) and a +1 probe for hasMore (gallery.ts:37-40,58,86,123); getLessonState limit 80 then 6 per task; student home limit 6; studio LIST_LIMIT 150 per source; group-reports pages 1000 with MAX_ROWS 50k guard.

No N+1 in the student-facing pages: gallery = 1 jobs query + 1 nickname query + ≤1 Storage sign call per 100 paths; lesson state = 3 parallel queries + 1 sign call; studio media = 2 queries + 1 sign + 1 profiles; group page = getGroup + listStudents (2 queries) + star stats (2 queries); teach index = groups + 1 members query.

The lazy poller's refund timings are consistent between TS and SQL: STORING_RECLAIM_AFTER_MS = 3 min (job-rules.ts:348) matches begin_job_storing's `interval '3 minutes'` (init.sql:634); submitted timeout 5/15 min and hard limit 60 min are only in TS (job-rules.ts:349-356) and apply via the job's own poll.

Money-safety of SQL grants: service_role has SELECT only on wallets and star_ledger (init.sql:371), all money changes go through security-definer functions granted only to service_role (init.sql:822-838); ledger is append-only by trigger (init.sql:289-301); wallet balance CHECK ≥ 0. Tests 002:114-122 confirm server cannot write wallets/ledger directly.

RLS helper functions wrap auth.uid() in `(select …)` so it is evaluated once per statement (init.sql:306-331, 382-422), the recommended Supabase pattern; the shared-gallery policy's `exists (groups … share_gallery)` is a cheap PK lookup per candidate row and is only evaluated for 24-row pages.

Text generations stay inside the 60 s function budget by design: RETRY_BUDGET_MS.text = 50 s and create 45 s (gateway.ts:187), AbortSignal.timeout per attempt; createTask marks `uncertain` on timeout and leaves the job queued for the 3-minute lazy refund instead of refunding immediately (generate.ts:343-348) — correct against double-spend of kie credits.

Student creation batch (teach/actions.ts:229-256) runs 5 createUser calls in parallel, well under Auth admin API limits; the auth.users triggers (handle_new_user + handle_user_meta_updated, group_budget.sql:81-102 and student_meta.sql:69-84) lock only the new student's own profile row, so they do not contend with the lesson.

Montage upload bypasses Vercel's 4.5 MB body limit correctly: signed upload URL straight to Storage (studio.ts:383), the server only verifies size/mime via list+Range request (studio.ts:439-453) and completes the pre-created 0★ job; stale uploads are refunded/closed per user (studio.ts:297-323) with a 10-row bound.

findings.title: Own per-IP login limiter (100/15 min) counts successful logins and all attempts — a 50-person room can lock itself out for 15 minutes
findings.evidence: actions.ts:43-46 calls takeAttempt(LOGIN_LIMITS.ip) before every sign-in, including the ones that succeed; only the account counter is reset on success (actions.ts:55). rate-limit.ts:21 sets ip = 100 attempts per 15 min (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64, bot/ratelimit.ts:47-53). The whole classroom shares one public IP [research: 'Classroom NAT']. When the counter is exhausted the student sees TOO_MANY = 'Подождите пару минут' (actions.ts:22) although the window is 15 minutes. The counter is DB-backed (rate_limit_hit under advisory lock, migration :136-150) so it is shared across all Vercel instances — the limit really is global for the room.
findings.scenario10: 10 students × (1 success + ~1 typo of a 17-character card password) ≈ 20-30 attempts in 2 minutes → far below 100. No impact.
findings.scenario50: 50 students × 1 success = 50 attempts before any mistake. Each wrong password (13-year-olds typing kiwi-raketa-sova-42 from a card; 30-50 % first-try error rate is realistic) adds one. ~75-100 attempts in the first 2 minutes; a second group in the same room within 15 minutes, or a few students re-logging after a phone lock, crosses 100 → EVERY further login from the room returns 'Слишком много попыток' for up to 15 minutes while the teacher has no unlock button. Lesson start stalls.
findings.fix: (1) Count only failures for the IP rule: keep takeAttempt before sign-in for the account rule, but for the IP rule check-without-increment first and increment only when signInWithPassword fails (add a `p_increment boolean` parameter to rate_limit_hit or call rate_limit_hit only in the error branch; a small race is acceptable here). (2) Raise LOGIN_LIMITS.ip to at least 300 per 15 min (IPv4) — brute-force protection still comes from the 20-per-account rule. (3) Make the message truthful and child-readable: 'Слишком много попыток входа с этого места. Подождите 15 минут или позовите ведущего.' (4) Document in setup.md that one room = one IP and what the limit means.

findings.title: Supabase /auth/v1/token per-IP bucket (30 burst, 1800/h) is shared by server-side sign-ins AND refreshes from Vercel egress IPs; a 429 on refresh after token expiry logs the student out
findings.evidence: Sign-in runs server-side with the publishable key (actions.ts:49, server.ts:18), so GoTrue keys the bucket on the Vercel function's egress IP, which is dynamic and undocumented in size [research: 'Vercel egress IP']. Refreshes go to the same per-IP bucket [research: 'Auth rate limit']. In auth-js, getClaims → getSession → __loadSession refreshes when the token is within EXPIRY_MARGIN_MS = 90 s of expiry (constants.js:13, GoTrueClient.js:2541-2547). A 429 is NOT in NETWORK_ERROR_CODES (fetch.js:32-34), so it is non-retryable: if the access token is still valid the session is preserved, but if it has already expired _removeSession() runs (GoTrueClient.js ~4310-4318) and the cookies are deleted → proxy.ts:58-61 redirects to /login. Each request builds a fresh client (server.ts:14, proxy.ts:38), so the per-client failure cooldown does not apply: every 5-second poll re-attempts the refresh during the 90 s margin, amplifying any 429 storm. Students who all logged in within the same 2 minutes also all refresh within the same 2 minutes one hour later. actions.ts:52 maps a 429 at sign-in to TOO_MANY with no retry.
findings.scenario10: 10 sign-ins in 2 min plus 10 refreshes an hour later are far inside a 30-burst bucket even if every call exits from one Vercel IP. No impact expected.
findings.scenario50: If 50 sign-ins cluster into ~30 s through one warm instance/egress IP, capacity is 30 + 15 refilled = 45 → the last 5-10 students get 'Слишком много попыток' and must retry blindly. One hour later the refresh wave repeats the same clustering; a 429 there while a student's token has just expired silently logs them out (redirect to /login mid-chat, polls return 401). Probability is medium (depends on undocumented Vercel egress IP pool) but the consequence is visible to several students at once.
findings.fix: (1) In login(): on error.status === 429 wait 1.5-3 s with jitter and retry signInWithPassword once before returning TOO_MANY; change the message to 'Сервер занят. Подождите 10 секунд и нажмите «Войти» ещё раз.' (2) Log { status: error.status, at: Date.now() } with console.error (no e-mail) so the first 50-person workshop produces evidence of how many 429s occur. (3) Teacher procedure in setup.md: log students in in two waves of ≤25 at least 1 minute apart; open the site 5 min early. (4) Do NOT move sign-in to the browser and do NOT enable Sb-Forwarded-For for this flow — the room's single IP would hit the same bucket harder [research: 'Classroom NAT']. (5) Keep JWT expiry at 1 h (lowering it multiplies refreshes against the same bucket). (6) On Pro, test whether PATCH /v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth rate_limit_token_refresh is honoured (unverified [research]).

findings.title: Per-account lockout (20 wrong passwords / 15 min) lets any classmate lock a peer out, and nobody can unlock
findings.evidence: Account rule: 20 attempts per login per 15 min (rate-limit.ts:19), checked at actions.ts:44 and reset only on a successful login (actions.ts:55). Logins are predictable: <group code>-<first name> (accounts.ts:55-64; the real group uses 770-naomi style, docs/course/770-status.md:27). There is no teacher action that calls rate_limit_reset for an account; resetStudentPassword (teach/actions.ts:300-315) sets a new password but leaves the counter, so after a reset the student can still be blocked for the rest of the window.
findings.scenario10: Teenagers in one room know each other's names; one student typing 20 wrong passwords into a neighbour's login (or a neighbour's phone autofill looping) blocks that student for 15 minutes; teacher's reset does not help. One student idle for a quarter of the lesson.
findings.scenario50: Same mechanism, more targets and more accidental triggers (shared devices, autofill with stale passwords). A handful of students blocked at once with the misleading 'Подождите пару минут' message.
findings.fix: (1) In resetStudentPassword call resetAttempts(LOGIN_LIMITS.account, studentEmail(login)) right after updateUserById, so a reset always unblocks. (2) Add a teacher button 'Снять блокировку входа' that calls resetAttempts for the account (audit it). (3) Consider a soft lock instead of a hard one: after 20 failures add a 30-s delay per attempt rather than a 15-min wall. (4) Tell the student the real wait time in the message.

findings.title: Teacher password reset revokes all of the student's sessions (GoTrue Logout) — student is kicked out within the hour with no explanation, and job polling keeps spinning on 401
findings.evidence: updateUserById(student.id, { password }) (teach/actions.ts:308) hits GoTrue adminUserUpdate, which calls user.UpdatePassword(tx, nil) (supabase/auth internal/api/admin.go:267-268); with sessionID == nil that function runs models.Logout(tx, u.ID) — 'log out user from all sessions' (internal/models/user.go:519-521, fetched 2026-11-08). The student's access token keeps verifying locally (getClaims is offline with asymmetric keys) until exp ≤ 1 h; the next refresh fails non-retryably → cookies removed → page navigations redirect to /login (proxy.ts:58-61). API polls get 401 (jobs route:25) but fetchJob returns null on any !ok (GenerateClient.ts:53) and useLiveJob keeps polling every 5 s forever (GenerateClient.ts:78-93) — the card shows 'в работе' indefinitely. For a chat send the student sees only 'Войдите, чтобы продолжить.' (messages.ts:40) with no link.
findings.scenario10: A student forgets the password after a break, the teacher resets it while the student's laptop is still logged in: the laptop works for up to an hour, then suddenly redirects to /login; any pending video card never updates. Confusing but one student.
findings.scenario50: Several resets per workshop are likely (lost cards). Same effect for each; the teacher does not know that a reset implies a forced re-login, and students report 'the site threw me out' during generation.
findings.fix: (1) In GenerateClient.fetchJob return a typed 'unauthorized' on 401 and let useLiveJob stop polling and show 'Сессия закончилась — войдите заново, задача продолжится' with a link to /login?next=<current path>. (2) Render errorMessages.unauthorized with a login link in GeneratePanel/QuizForm notices. (3) In the teacher UI next to 'Сбросить пароль' add the sentence 'Ученика выкинет из кабинета в течение часа — пусть войдёт заново с новым паролем', and note it in setup.md. (4) Optional: after reset, show the new password immediately and tell the teacher to hand it over before the hour ends.

findings.title: Session cookies are neither httpOnly nor Secure (ssr defaults) although the app has no browser Supabase client and allows 'unsafe-inline' scripts
findings.evidence: Neither createServerClient call passes cookieOptions (server.ts:18, proxy.ts:38), so @supabase/ssr applies DEFAULT_COOKIE_OPTIONS = { path:'/', sameSite:'lax', httpOnly:false, maxAge: 400 days } (constants.js:4-10) — no Secure flag, JS-readable. No createBrowserClient or client-side supabase-js import exists anywhere in app/, components/ or lib/ outside lib/server (grep 2026-11-08), so nothing in the browser needs to read the cookie. The platform CSP uses script-src 'unsafe-inline' (next.config.ts:39), so any future XSS (e.g. in rendered model output) could exfiltrate the refresh token, which never expires by default [research: 'Refresh token rotation'].
findings.scenario10: No functional impact; latent risk that a single XSS gives an attacker a permanent session of a student (or the teacher/admin, whose session can create students and move stars).
findings.scenario50: Same latent risk, larger blast radius (50 students' long-lived refresh tokens). Not a lesson-breaker, but the owner wants to sell the platform; this is a cheap item that a buyer's security review will flag.
findings.fix: Pass cookieOptions: { httpOnly: true, secure: !isDevelopment(), sameSite: 'lax' } in both createServerClient calls (server.ts and proxy.ts). applyServerStorage spreads cookieOptions over the defaults for every chunk (cookies.js:223-230), so chunked cookies inherit the flags. Verify locally that login, refresh and logout still work (they are all server-side).

findings.title: Logout signs out every device of the login (global scope) — a student using phone + laptop loses both
findings.evidence: logout() calls supabase.auth.signOut() with no options (actions.ts:69); auth-js default is scope: 'global' (GoTrueClient.js:3417), which revokes all refresh tokens of the user. The DB shows users already holding up to 4 concurrent sessions (auth.sessions, read-only check 2026-11-08). The other device keeps working only until its access token expires (≤ 1 h), then is redirected to /login.
findings.scenario10: A student logs out on the classroom laptop at the end; their phone, which they use to watch the result later, silently stops working within an hour and asks for the card again.
findings.scenario50: Same, more often; also two students sharing one card on two devices (not intended, but happens) log each other out.
findings.fix: Use supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' }) in logout(); keep the implicit global sign-out in the disabled-account branch (actions.ts:59) where revoking everything is desired. Mention in setup.md that a card works on several devices and that 'Выйти' affects only that device.

findings.title: Leaked-password protection: status log says ON, live project says OFF — settings and documentation disagree
findings.evidence: Supabase security advisor for project workshop (2026-11-08): 'auth_leaked_password_protection — Leaked password protection is currently disabled' (WARN). docs/course/770-status.md:16 marks 'защита от утёкших паролей включена' as done. If it is enabled, GoTrue's checkPasswordStrength (admin.go:239, :453) also runs for admin createUser/updateUserById, so a generated three-word password that appears in HIBP would make createStudents put that student into `failed` (teach/actions.ts:246-252) and resetStudentPassword throw 'server_error'.
findings.scenario10: No lesson impact either way; the risk is only that the owner believes a protection is active when it is not.
findings.scenario50: Same. If the owner enables it later, expect rare single-student failures in batch creation (handled) and in password reset (surfaces as 'Что-то пошло не так' — teacher just clicks again).
findings.fix: Decide one way and align: either enable it in Authentication → Sign In / Providers → Passwords and keep the status note, or untick the status note. If enabled, make resetStudentPassword retry once with a new generated password when updateUserById returns 422 weak_password/pwned.

findings.title: Login failures and 429s are not logged anywhere — no evidence to debug a bad workshop start
findings.evidence: The only logging in actions.ts is none (grep for console.* returns nothing); audit() is used for teacher actions only. A Supabase 429 (actions.ts:52) and a wrong password are both returned as plain strings with no server log line. Unified logs for the project currently show only pgbouncer/postgres sources (query 2026-11-08), so Vercel function logs are the sole place where auth failures could appear.
findings.scenario10: If a student cannot log in, the owner cannot tell afterwards whether it was a typo, our limiter or Supabase's bucket.
findings.scenario50: The first big workshop is the only chance to measure how many server-side sign-ins hit Supabase 429 (unresolved research item); without a log line the measurement is lost.
findings.fix: Add console.error('login: failed', { status: error.status, code: error.code, limiter: 'ip'|'account'|null }) in actions.ts for 429/limiter outcomes only (never log the e-mail or password); optionally write a daily aggregate to the audit table.

findings.title: Polish: dead /admin prefix, logged-in user not redirected away from /login, TOO_MANY wording
findings.evidence: PROTECTED includes '/admin' (proxy.ts:14) and next.config.ts:83 sets headers for it, but no app/(platform)/admin or app/admin directory exists (find 2026-11-08); safeNext (actions.ts:27) accepts only /app and /teach. A signed-in user visiting /login sees the form again (page.tsx has no getUser check) and a second login simply overwrites the cookie, leaving the old session orphaned. TOO_MANY says 'пару минут' while the limiter window is 15 min (rate-limit.ts:19,21).
findings.scenario10: Minor confusion only: a student who bookmarked /login re-enters the password unnecessarily.
findings.scenario50: Same; the misleading wait time causes repeated retries that consume the IP counter (see AUTH-1).
findings.fix: Remove '/admin' from PROTECTED and headers until an admin area exists (or add it to safeNext); in login/page.tsx redirect to homePath(user) when getUser() is non-null; make TOO_MANY state the real wait.

findings.title: Docs say the Supabase project is in Frankfurt; the live project is eu-west-1 (Ireland)
findings.evidence: Supabase list_projects (2026-11-08): workshop → region eu-west-1. setup.md:18: 'регион ЕС (Frankfurt)'. Both are EU, so no compliance impact; only the doc is wrong.
findings.scenario10: None.
findings.scenario50: None; a buyer reading the docs gets a wrong fact.
findings.fix: Change setup.md:18 to 'регион ЕС (eu-west-1, Ирландия)'.

okChecked: Open-redirect protection on ?next= (actions.ts:25-28): only paths matching ^/(app|teach)(/|?|$), rejects //, backslashes and absolute URLs; proxy.toLogin (proxy.ts:21-28) builds next from pathname+search, so /app/lessons/2?step=3 round-trips correctly.

Server-side auth caching hazard: proxy.ts:49-51 copies the Cache-Control/Expires/Pragma headers passed by @supabase/ssr setAll onto the response, and redirects carry the refreshed cookies (proxy.ts:58-61); lib/server/supabase/server.ts:23-31 swallows cookie writes from Server Components per the official pattern. API routes answer with cache-control: no-store (generate/route.ts:58, jobs route:33). Matches Supabase guidance [research: 'Server-side auth caching hazard'].

JWT verification is offline: getClaims verifies the signature with JWKS cached per process in GLOBAL_JWKS for JWKS_TTL = 10 min (auth-js GoTrueClient.js:48-60, 5418-5450, constants.js:51), so with asymmetric keys neither proxy.ts:55 nor dal/auth.ts:58 calls Supabase Auth per request. Caveat for the owner: confirm Project Settings → JWT Keys shows ECC/RSA (the sandbox could not reach the project's jwks.json); with a legacy HS256 secret every request would fall back to a network getUser() call (GoTrueClient.js getClaims fallback).

Authorization is in every Route Handler and Server Action, not in proxy: authorize() in app/api/generate/route.ts:25, app/api/jobs/[id]/route.ts:18, lessons/[n]/actions.ts:40, teach/actions.ts (authorize(STAFF_ROLES)); role comes from profiles.role, never from JWT metadata (dal/auth.ts:62-75); disabled profiles are treated as logged out (dal/auth.ts:75) and the login action signs them out immediately (actions.ts:57-61).

Refresh-token rotation race with 5 tabs/polls: all concurrent requests carry the same refresh token; GoTrue's 10 s reuse interval and the 'parent of the active token returns the active token' rule [research: 'Refresh token rotation'] mean a long /api/generate request (50 s) whose Set-Cookie arrives late cannot invalidate the family; auth-js dedupes concurrent refreshes inside one client (refreshingDeferred, GoTrueClient.js:4197-4199) and keeps the session on 'refresh_token_already_used' (GoTrueClient.js:3685). No random logouts expected at 10 or 50.

Same login on two devices: independent sessions (live DB shows up to 4 sessions per user, 0 time-boxed sessions); both keep working for the whole lesson; 'Single session per user' is not enabled [research].

Session expiry mid-lesson: access token 1 h, refresh triggered automatically by proxy.ts:55 on any matched request when < 90 s remain (EXPIRY_MARGIN_MS); with polling every 5 s (GenerateClient.ts:12) the refresh happens while the student works. Client state survives: typed prompt and uploads are React state, chat thread is in localStorage (GeneratePanel.tsx:100), quiz answers are useState (QuizForm.tsx:51) — a 401 shows a notice but loses nothing (apart from AUTH-4 polling polish).
Token refresh load: ≈ 1 refresh per student per hour → 10 or 50 per lesson vs 1800/h bucket — negligible [research: 'Token refresh load']. JWT expiry should stay at 1 h.

Our login counters are correct across Fluid instances: stored in Postgres (private.rate_limit_hits) under pg_advisory_xact_lock per key, keyed by HMAC of login/IP (no PII), self-cleaning; fail-open on DB error is deliberate and documented (rate-limit.ts:37-45); covered by supabase/tests/004_security_hardening.test.sql:56-62 and :88-90 (clients cannot call the functions).
